keyVerseText: And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses, one of his young men, answered and said, My lord Moses, forbid them.
rootMeaning: The root word בָּחוּר (bâchûwr) conveys the idea of a young man who is chosen or selected, emphasizing not just youth but also a status of being set apart or preferred. The feminine plural form בְּחֻרוֹת (bᵉchurôwth) carries this sense collectively, referring to youth as a group. This root meaning enriches the English gloss 'young men' by highlighting an element of selection or choice, suggesting these are not just any youths but those distinguished or appointed for a particular role or purpose.
usageInScripture: The word בְּחֻרוֹת appears three times in Scripture, consistently referring to youth either collectively or as individuals. It is translated mostly as 'of thy youth' twice, indicating a connection to the period of early life or vigor, and once as 'one of his young men,' denoting a specific young person serving in a role. This consistent usage underscores the word's focus on youthfulness combined with a sense of responsibility or selection, whether abstractly as a stage of life or concretely as a servant or attendant.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding בְּחֻרוֹת as 'chosen youth' invites reflection on how God values and appoints the young in His purposes. Youth is not merely a time of life but a season of potential and divine selection, reminding believers that God calls individuals at every age to serve Him. This word also points to the faithfulness required of the young, who are often called to leadership and service in Scripture. Recognizing this enriches our view of spiritual maturity as something that begins early and is marked by being chosen and set apart by God’s grace.
keyVerseReflection: In Numbers 11:28, the phrase 'one of his young men' translates בְּחֻרוֹת to identify Joshua as a chosen attendant of Moses. This highlights Joshua’s role not just as a youth but as a selected servant entrusted with responsibility. The word conveys Joshua’s status as part of a faithful, divinely appointed group, emphasizing how God raises up young leaders to carry forward His mission even in challenging times.
